planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in shade to part shade; Rollissonii is an old, narrow-leaved form of drooping leucothoe distinguished from the species mainly by its slimmer, more pointed foliage on the same gracefully arching stems.

directions: Rollissonii is a long-cultivated, narrow-leaved selection of native drooping leucothoe, set apart from the standard species mostly by its slimmer, more tapered foliage carried on the same cascading, layered stems. Small white, urn-shaped flowers hang in short racemes along the undersides of the branches in late spring, and the glossy dark green summer leaves often take on bronze-purple tones through winter. Give it consistently moist, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in shade to part shade, since the fine foliage scorches readily in strong sun or dry conditions. Its weeping, fine-textured habit makes a useful foil for broader-leaved rhododendrons and azaleas in a shaded woodland border.
sources: Dirr's Manual of Woody Landscape Plants

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; avoid soggy sites and heavy afternoon sun. Nipmuck is one of the compact mountain laurel selections bred by Richard Jaynes, part of the same Connecticut breeding effort that produced 'Sarah'.

directions: Nipmuck is one of the compact mountain laurel selections bred by Richard Jaynes, part of the same Connecticut breeding program that produced 'Sarah'. It carries pink-tinged buds that open to lighter pink flowers in early summer against the species' typical glossy, leathery evergreen foliage, held on a dense, well-branched frame more compact than wild-collected mountain laurel. Site it in dappled woodland shade in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, and avoid soggy ground or heavy afternoon sun which both stress the shallow root system. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.
